sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A mathematics or related bachelor’s degree, overall GPA 3.0 and mathematics GPA 3.0, with abstract algebra,
linear algebra, and advanced calculus/analysis preparation. Admission remains selective. International
applicants are eligible. [s1]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through KU Graduate Admissions; prepare a separate textbook list and identify referees. No advance
supervisor agreement is required. International GTA candidates need speaking-test evidence even when their
US degree establishes admission-level English proficiency. [s1] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor commitment before applying; a research adviser is normally selected after qualifying
examinations in years 2-3. Admissions contact: Michelle Morrison, michmor@ku.edu. [s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use KU Graduate Admissions. Referee requests can precede submission; submitted letters are linked when the
application is submitted. Follow the mathematics-specific transcript and textbook-list instructions. [s1] [s4]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Central applications for 2027 opened September 8, 2026, but the mathematics page’s January 5/6 conflict is
unresolved and its stipend is labeled 2025-26. [s1] [s4]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
For full admission proficiency: old TOEFL 80 with each section 20, new TOEFL 4.5 with each section 4.5; IELTS
6.5 with each section 6; PTE 60 with each section 55. Official scores are required and must remain within two
years at processing; MyBest and IELTS One Skill Retake are not accepted. GTA speaking eligibility separately
requires old TOEFL speaking 22/new 4.5 or IELTS speaking 7. [s1] [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
An earned bachelor’s degree from an accredited US institution establishes full admission English proficiency.
Whether an in-progress UChicago degree suffices at application is not explicit. This degree provision does NOT
waive the international GTA speaking-test requirement. [s1] [s3]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required. The department explicitly instructs applicants not to put GRE scores in the CV. Handling of
voluntarily submitted score reports is not established. [s1]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload scans/copies of registrar-issued official transcripts. Documents labeled unofficial, advising reports, or
web grade reports do not satisfy the department’s instruction. Final official records are sent directly after
admission. [s1]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Required separate list of textbooks, including authors, used in mathematics courses beyond calculus; a
transcript alone does not replace this list. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Full course descriptions are not listed in the public checklist; the separate textbook-and-author list is explicitly
required. Whether the portal requests further course details is unverified. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Historical 2025-26 GTA academic-year stipend: USD 20,084.01, approximately August 18-May 15, for 20
hours/week. Package includes full tuition, 75% of health-insurance premium, the wellness fee, and 50% of
required student fees; international-student fees are excluded. This is not a verified 2027-28 rate. [s1]
Years of support [Standing rule]
All admitted PhD students receive a six-year funding package, subject to its conditions. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD students are eligible for departmental assistantships; GTA speaking qualification remains
mandatory. The Self Graduate Fellowship is restricted to domestic applicants. [s1]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
GTA duties are 20 hours/week; continued support depends on academic and employment requirements.
Summer research support can be available for up to three summers after both qualifying examinations and
selection of an adviser; availability and amount are conditional. [s1]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate departmental financial-aid application; admission materials determine merit-based support. [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
The Self Graduate Fellowship advertises USD 40,000/year for four years for 2026-27, plus
development/startup/textbook allowances, but is domestic-only and should not be budgeted by this F-1
applicant. Departmental summer support and travel support may be available. [s1]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 100 for international applicants; domestic USD 65. [s5]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Mathematics states it does not offer fee waivers. The domestic Self Fellowship waiver route is not applicable to
an international F-1 applicant. [s1]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Yunfeng Jiang
Moduli of maps and sheaves, enumerative invariants, Donaldson-Thomas and Vafa-Witten theory, surface
singularities and deformation theory. [faculty1] [faculty1a]
Black-Babcock Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · A virtual PGL_r/SL_r correspondence for projective surfaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Hai Long (Hailong) Dao
Commutative algebra, local singularities, syzygies and categories of modules, with connections to algebraic
geometry and K-theory. [faculty5] [faculty5a]
Professor; CV lists Spring 2027 SLMath visit, so confirm timing for any visit or research contact.
Research evidence: 2026 · Ulrich split rings
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Daniel Hernández
Singularities in positive characteristic, Frobenius methods, local cohomology, differential operators and convex
methods in birational geometry. [faculty7] [faculty7a]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 · Bernstein's inequality and holonomicity for certain singular rings
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Emily E. Witt
Commutative algebra and singularity theory; Frobenius thresholds, local cohomology, differential operators,
and computational algebra. [faculty9] [faculty9a] [faculty_witt_date]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024, publication date cross-checked on coauthor Hernández page · Bernstein's inequality and
holonomicity for certain singular rings
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.

Complex geometry
Ruijie Yang
Hodge theory and D-modules, singularities, birational geometry, abelian varieties and theta divisors; also links
to geometric representation theory. [faculty3] [faculty3a]
Assistant Professor since 2024; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Higher multiplier ideals
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
